research.arcana.root.text:
A sudden burst of inspiration, key insights that make clear the meaning of these scribbled notes... the way forward is unclear, but I know that this is the start of something magical.
I'll write down my research in this book: the Arcanum, with all of the old notes stored inside for reference.
research.arcana.aspects.text:
My new perspective has enabled me to understand the ramblings of these scribbled notes.{~sep}Among them are key insights into the workings of reality.
All matter is composed of Aspects, the fundamental building blocks of reality. Aspects come in a number of varieties, about {c3}{$numOfAspects}{r}, each of which corresponds to some concept.
All aspects are composed of two simpler aspects, with the exception of the six Primal aspects: {aspect:air}{c6}aer{r} (air), {aspect:earth}{c2}terra{r} (earth), {aspect:water}{c1}aqua{r} (water), {aspect:fire}{c4}ignis{r} (fire), {aspect:order}{c7}ordo{r} (order), and {aspect:entropy}perditio (entropy).
The chemical elements are, unintuitively, also fundamental building blocks. Elements and aspects are two "lenses" with which to view and modify the world, and different things lend themselves to a different lens.
These aspects can also apparently be isolated into solid-like, fluid-like, and gaseous forms. Crystals are solid, and result from overflows of a particular aspect in the aura. The aura, in turn, is made up of the more gaseous vis form, and is almost entirely uniform, except around nodes, which produce a constant supply of primal vis.
Finally, equipment can supposedly be used to purify it into a fluid state known as essentia. The notes were frustratingly vague on this... the equipment seems both too complex to infer from diagrams, yet so commmonplace that they neglected to explain properly. Their most powerful tools relied on it extensively, seemingly forcing me to reinvent their basic practices myself.
research.arcana.flux.desc: No such thing as free lunch
research.arcana.flux.stage.1:
My new perspective has enabled me to understand the ramblings of these scribbled notes.{~sep}Among them were various vague warnings of "flux", "taint", and "warp", as consequences for mishandling magic.
Flux is a kind of pollution of the aura, produced through wasteful alchemy, or inefficient equipment. While nothing arcane is without risks, a buildup of flux can pose serious risks to yourself and the world.
Taint being one of them. Some sort of corruption, or parasite, or {i}something{i}, that works its way through the world, and twists living beings into horrific monsters when left to its own devices; feeding on the flux created by ambitious or negligent alchemists.
And while I couldn't fully parse the notes on warp... the dark rituals and grim compulsions that surrounded it were certainly enough to provide a bad first impression.
If I don't study these risks, how am I supposed to protect myself from them? I should get a look of this "flux" myself. A small amount should be perfectly manageable.
research.arcana.flux.stage.2: ...that was probably a mistake. Everything just {i}feels{i} off here. I would do well not to let it grow much higher, lest it start producing physical effects more serious than a headache and stomachache... ugh, I don't even want to know what warp feels like.
research.arcana.silverwood_trees.text:
Silverwood trees are wide and stubby, noticeable for their bright colouration, high rarity, and incredible magical potential.
Every author of these notes could agree on one thing: silverwood trees are the key to many inventions. Their wood is one of the few things capable of resisting {i}purified essentia{r}; every part of the plant is completely immune to, and even repels, taint; and occasionally, their growth can even create a new Pure Node.
It should go without saying that growing and studying these trees wherever possible is a high priority.
research.arcana.greatwood_trees.text:
Greatwood trees are towering, easily taller than any kind of mundane wood that I have come across.
Their wood is receptive to vis, especially {aspect:earth} and {aspect:water}, which may help explain how minerals and fluids are transported up their vast trunks.
While rarer than other trees, being found sparsely across various habitats, once found, they are hard to miss. A single tree should provide enough wood for anything I could need, and enough saplings to make that certain.
Their magical nature will make them quite useful in future work.
research.arcana.hungry_nodes.text:
Nodes come in a variety of forms, some of which pose particular risks to the aspiring thaumaturge; Hungry Nodes are a prime example.{~sep}Rather than generating vis from nothing, as every other kind is happy to do, hungry nodes instead consume their surrounding terrain, holding onto some amount of it's aspects as vis.
Even without special equipment, this can be clearly seen from the matter being drawn into them, and the accretion disc surrounding them.
These nodes pose a very direct, physical risk to anyone who wishes to use them. At the same time, they provide a prime opportunity: to feed them with matter, and create a powerful vis battery to take advantage of.
...they pose a difficult question too. How {i}do{r} other nodes create vis? Where does it come from? One cannot create energy, only convert it from matter; could other nodes simply be openings to hungry nodes elsewhere?
research.arcana.eldritch_nodes.text:
Nodes come in a variety of forms, some of which pose particular risks to the aspiring thaumaturge; even among these, Eldritch Nodes are unique in their ability to profoundly manipulate your emotions.{~sep}While they are just as transparent to the naked eye as any other node, their presence can be felt by the icy aura that surrounds them, the shiver that runs through you, the terror that swells should you make eye contact. These nodes... hate you, somehow, and they make their feelings known.
I believe they have some impact on what the notes referred to as {c3}warp{r}, too, worsening it within their presence.
Careful observation shows their true shape: a pulsating eye. What they are looking for, I cannot know.
research.arcana.nodal_geodes.text:
When venturing underground for resources, I came across a geode filled with vis crystals, with a node at its centre. Such {i}Nodal Geodes{r} are a valuable source of otherwise-sparse crystals.
Unlike surface nodes, each geode is attuned to only one kind of primal vis, which permeates through the rock that makes it up, alongside condensing into crystals. The node within will be especially potent in that aspect.
Given a method of viewing nodes, finding nodal geodes should not be too difficult, but reaching them might be a chore.
research.arcana.primordial_pearl.text:
For the first time I find myself with a puzzle that I do not believe should be solved.{~sep}This object refuses to take a distinct form, and while it is conceptually complex, only contains huge amounts of primal aspects. These aspects do not act like the ordinary primals.
Every one of my various theories falls apart every moment this changes form. I would suggest it might be consciously obfuscating itself, but doing so leaves it perfectly simple and easy to understand - for one, fleeting moment, until all clarity is lost once more.
It stays constant only in one aspect: the aspects it contains. It... must have existed before compound aspects themselves, if there was such a time? Or perhaps it exists in some other way, one that cannot be expressed as aspects entirely?

crimson_equipment.name: Crimson Equipment
crimson_equipment.text: The Crimson Cultists have devised a number of interesting weapons, most of which incorporate their knowledge of the {i}Projecting{r} enchantment into their design quite effectively.

projecting.name: Projecting
projecting.text:
A curious enchantment applicable to rings. When worn, a projecting ring creates a spectral presence a short distance from myself, extending my attack and placement range slightly. Rings that already hold strong magic can only support lower levels.
The enchanted books found in Crimson settlements have a horrible sense of fear around them... I don't believe the cultists created these through ordinary means.

crimson_blade.name: Crimson Blade
crimson_blade.text: The Crimson Blade extends its reach not by being physically longer - in fact, it's somewhat shorter than an ordinary sword - but by creating a magical projectile that extends a short distance from the user. This projectile deals the same amount of damage as the blade's physical damage, but in the form of magical damage, and is only cast if the blade does not physically connect with its opponent.

crimson_longbow.name: Crimson Longbow
crimson_longbow.text: Arrows fired from a Crimson Longbow have the strange property of being capable of phasing through certain thin materials, such as iron bars or glass panes. This occurs even if the arrow is already magical (say, spectral or tipped). The Cultists seem to have designed their outposts around this, giving their Archers an undeniable advantage from a distance.

crimson_leech.name: Crimson Leech
crimson_leech.text:
{c}Wet. Writhing. Warm.
{c}Threads of {i}something{r}.
Flexible and malleable and it stains and it stinks and it snakes throughout. Bulbous growths and- tongues? No, just blades? Something between.
{c}What a horrific weapon. It-
{~sep}From the start. This thing resembles a kind of whip, though one made largely of largely-living tissue. How organic it {i}actually{r} is, I cannot be certain, but it seems capable of some metabolism? It can stretch and reach a distance much further than it appears it should, and can transfer some lifeforce back to the user, though it seems "eager" for some of its own.
Whatever magic went into this must have been powerful, something they have neglected to show me so far. Perhaps I am lucky of that.

research.arcana.wandcraft.stage.1:
To continue any further, I'll need some way of directly manipulating vis. The tools once used for this were wands, constructed from a wide variety of materials that combine to create powerful magic.
Constructing a simple wand is as simple as capping off a stick with purpose-built metal wand caps, the same design reusable as I improve my materials and skills.
{i}Some{r} notes seem to refer to the use of a special glove, directly grabbing the vis with my hands; constructing such a thing seems impossible with what I have available, however.
research.arcana.wandcraft.stage.2:
Now, I have a real way to control magic. Soon, I'll be tapping on walls and whispering spells to open hidden gateways...
But first, I'll need to charge my wand with energy, by draining a node of it's power.
research.arcana.nodes.text:
At the start of my journey, I was given a glimpse of knowledge from a source of magic. These sources - or nodes, as I have come to know them - seem to be scattered across the world, constantly {i}creating{r} new energy. Something I believed to be impossible.{~sep}Nodes aren't quite uniform. Different nodes are attuned to different aspects, only producing those, and holding onto larger amounts of them.
Some nodes are brighter than others, producing vis more rapidly and holding onto more.
I can drain their vis into a wand by holding right-click. As long as I don't completely drain them, their aspects will simply replenish over time.
Fully emptying one can damage it, lowering it's aspect caps - or worse, paling it - so I should be careful.{~sep}A few of them seem to act... strangely. Sucking in terrain, corrupting nearby crystals, emitting a depressing aura... I would do well to study these properly.
research.arcana.arcane_crafting.stage.1:
The regular crafting table, while immensely useful, is simply not capable of handling vis in the way I require.
It should only require some slight tweaks - a touch of my wand's magic - to bring it up to par.
research.arcana.arcane_crafting.stage.2:
An Arcane Crafting Table is capable of everything it's ordinary variant is capable of, but can additionally craft magical items that require vis, supplied by my wand.
One such critical item is the Goggles of Revealing, which makes visible the vis around me.
When the goggles are worn, nodes become brighter and visible through terrain, and I can see the aspects contained within them.
Of course, further investigation into arcane devices is in order. I'll store this in the {c3}Artifice{r} tab of the Arcanum, accessible by selecting the goggles icon on the left.
research.arcana.research.stage.1: I can't go off the notes of long-dead magicians forever. I'll need a proper environment for my work; for testing theories, constructing theorems, and cross-referencing clues. I need a Research Table.
research.arcana.research.stage.2:
Now I have a proper space to do my work.
Many insights and items will require me to sit down at a research table and complete a {i}research puzzle{i}. The exact puzzle will depend on what I'm trying to learn about. By clicking on the puzzle requirement with paper and Scribing Tools on me, I can get a Research Note to place inside the table and start working on.{~sep}The basic puzzle, {i}Chemistry{i}, requires me to connect a set of aspects on a hexagonal grid.
Each note starts with a somewhat-random amount of each primal aspect. I can combine two aspects (if there exists a compound of them) by placing them at the bottom of the sidebar, and pressing '+'. I can also place aspects on the grid by left clicking; both use up the amount on that note. Compound aspects connect to their components (and vice versa, components to their compounds).
Once all pre-placed aspects are connected, the puzzle is solved. If I make a mistake, I can right click on the grid to remove an aspect; it is not returned to the note, though, so if I'm too wasteful, I may need to restart with a new note.
I should give this a go now.
research.arcana.research.stage.3:
This puzzle isn't too hard, though I can picture more complex items requiring more effort, with more complex aspects.
I should keep in mind that the {c3}Aspects of Magic{r} page displays all aspect combinations, in case I get stuck.
research.arcana.node_channelling.stage.1: While there are theoretically infinite nodes out there, I would prefer not to damage the ones nearby. To keep nodes bright and powerful, I will need to work on my node tapping technique.
research.arcana.node_channelling.stage.2:
Observing the way vis flows through different materials has allowed me to enhance the way I drain nodes.
Draining a node will now always leave it with 1 vis in each aspect, preferring to drain another, unless all aspects only have 1 vis. The chance of an aspect cap decreasing when drained fully is lower.
As a nice side-effect, draining vis now occurs much faster.
research.arcana.node_channelling_2.stage.1:
I'm sure I can do better than that.
With my better wands and increased knowledge, I should be able to control nodes to a far greater degree than... this.
research.arcana.node_channelling_2.stage.2:
Now, I can pull vis from nodes even faster, approaching the speed at which vis diffuses in air. Additionally, draining a node completely of a single aspect no longer has a chance of paling it. Fully draining multiple, however, still might.
I do wonder if I could increase the rate of recharge by submerging the node... or if I can alter it to become more powerful in some other way...
This will require further investigation.
research.arcana.auromancy.stage.1: This wood-and-iron wand isn't always going to cut it. Really, it's a terrible, glorified vis battery, with few ways to put it's magic to good use. Surely I can build something better?
research.arcana.auromancy.stage.2:
Gold is certainly an improvement over iron, but it doesn't take a genius to know that. Even ordinary enchanting prefers it over everything. The use of a magical wood is also fairly straightforward, though the proper techniques less so.
I believe some dedicated study towards wands and vis manipulation is in order. I'll store this in the {c3}Auromancy{r} tab of the Arcanum, accessible by selecting the wand icon on the left.
research.arcana.alchemy.stage.1:
Like the mundane elements, I will benefit by learning to separate and combine aspects, and the simplest method available to me to do so is plain old heat.
Of course, magic must be used to catalyze this breakdown, and no mundane material could possibly handle the heat required - but a flick of my wand should upgrade a regular cauldron to do just that.
research.arcana.alchemy.stage.2:
A Crucible can be used to melt down items into their constituent aspects. When filled with water and placed over a heat source (like fire, lava, or magma), anything thrown inside will be dissolved, and their aspects added to the water-essentia solution.
Actually purifying this essentia into a usable form is far beyond me, and will require dedicated equipment, but that's not to say it's useless in its current form; a variety of alchemical recipes can be performed with it.
If I throw a catalyst for an alchemy recipe I know into a crucible (and it contains all the required aspects), instead of being broken down, it'll absorb those aspects and be transformed into something new.
One basic application of this is Nitor: a stable and bright flame, created from coal and light.
I can empty a crucible by sneak-right-clicking on it, releasing all of its currently stored aspects. If it has no aspects (only water), I can also empty it with a bucket.
I should note that, since blocks and other entities know no alchemy, items they drop will {i}always{i} be broken down; also, that my Goggles of Revealing allow me to see the aspects stored inside.
I believe some dedicated study of alchemy is in order. I'll store this in the {c3}Alchemy{r} tab of the Arcanum, accessible by selecting the crucible icon on the left.
research.arcana.research_expertise.stage.1:
Performing more research will teach me more about the research process itself.
With a little practical experience, I should be able to simplify the process, and offset the increasing difficulty of these puzzles.
research.arcana.research_expertise.stage.2: I'm getting better at this.{~sep}Holding shift while hovering over an aspect in the research table will now show it's components. Additionally, removing an aspect from the chemistry grid has a {c3}25%{r} chance of returning it to the note.
research.arcana.research_mastery.desc: You can never know all the facts.
research.arcana.research_mastery.stage.1: There's always more to learn, yet more exciting opportunities to chase after - and my slow, inefficient research is holding me back.
research.arcana.research_mastery.stage.2: No matter how hard I work, how long I try, how much focus and effort I put in - my work is never finished.{~sep}Removing an aspect from the chemistry grid now has a {c3}50%{r} chance of returning it to the note. Notes also start out with more aspects.
research.arcana.tome_of_sharing.stage.1:
So far, it has been highly convenient to have my knowledge bound to my mind, persisting after death and across any copies of this book. This is less true when trying to share my work with friends.
I {i}would{r} simply write down the solutions to every puzzle I know; sadly, I've forgotten most of them, and others (like fieldwork) I might not be able to describe on paper easily. Besides, a magical solution seems more fun to implement.
research.arcana.tome_of_sharing.stage.2:
Enchanting another copy of the Arcanum to copy knowledge from my mind in a highly readable format was surprisingly simple. Perhaps I should be worried about that.
When a Tome of Sharing is used by any player when crouched, they will have their research progress added. When another player uses it normally, all puzzles stored in the book are completed for them.
The tome does not automatically complete research entries, and will not skip item or XP requirements; only puzzles.
research.arcana.crystal_farmer.stage.1:
Scouting the surface for the occasional node and digging tunnels underground for geodes are not sustainable or renewable sources of vis crystals.
Given their importance in even basic magic, I need a way to grow new ones.
research.arcana.crystal_farmer.stage.2:
By creating a sturdy {i}cluster seed{r}, I can grow new crystals.
Small clusters grow in the presence of a node with their aspect, draining from it to gain mass. Once fully grown, a cluster will drop at least 2 crystals.
The recipe works for all primal aspects, swapping {aspect:air} and the catalyst for the appropriate aspect and crystal.
I could not get seeds made from non-primal aspects to grow; perhaps due to their absence in the aura.
research.arcana.aura_crystallization.stage.1:
My ability to manipulate the aura is limited by the lack of any form of direct influence on it.
Just like any other concept, the aura has a corresponding aspect, {aspect:aura} Auram. But this one does not appear in any physical substance I know of; while it is a fairly straightforward compound, it refuses to be defined in terms of anything but itself.
Perhaps it lies too close to the boundary between different systems of aspects, not fully under my own domain...
But still, like any other aspect, it can be formed into crystals. If I could force a cluster seed into existence, it would provide me with a sustainable source of this aspect.
research.arcana.aura_crystallization.stage.2:
While the recipe I've formulated seems perfectly valid, actually performing it would be dangerous; the essentia will begin to boil off as flux before the necessary amount can be reached.
That said, if I can perform it just once, I should be able to use its crystals to create further seeds easily.
Auram Clusters demand large amounts of random aspects from nodes to grow, damaging and possibly destroying them if they don't get what they want.

flux_meter.title: Measuring Flux
stages:
With access to more capable materials, I should look towards creating a device capable of measuring local flux directly.
The spread of flux is complex and unpredictable, better to know for certain than to going off gut feeling.

The design of the Flux Meter is surprisingly simple for its utility. When held, it displays the local flux around me, as a bar that fills the meter. I can view an exact number by pressing shift.
If the flux level were to exceed {c3}100{r}, the maximum the meter can display, it begins to flash white. It would be a mistake to let it reach so high.
Additionally, to help keep things under control, I'll keep track of the source of my flux production on the following pages, and perhaps even do something about it.

research.arcana.artifice_root.text:
The study of {i}artifice{r}, the construction of magical devices through arcane crafting, will be documented here.
The Goggles of Revealing recipe from {c3}Fundamentals{r} is included here for completeness.
research.arcana.arcane_stone.text:
Arcane Stone is a fairly simple application of arcane crafting. It looks nice, it's stronger than ordinary stone, and may be useful in further crafting.
I can use it to make pedestals, which put a single item on display.
Arcane Stone Bricks can be created through crafting or stonecutting.
research.arcana.paving_stones.stage.1: My home could do with a fair few magical upgrades. Improving my mobility inside and increasing its protection are among my top priorities.
research.arcana.paving_stones.stage.2: Easier to walk along a flat surface than a rough cliff edge, and even moreso to walk along some enchanted floor tiles. The enchantment on the Paving Stones of Travel boost my speed and jump height when I walk on top.
research.arcana.paving_stones.stage.3:
Like a fence, the Paving Stones of Warding will keep out hostile monsters, but also allow me to walk over them unaffected.
I should keep in mind that any ranged attack can still pass by, and that protecting an area is worthless if monsters can simply spawn inside.
Additionally, monsters forced on top of Paving Stones of Warding will fall through them, just as they would any other block.

mundane_jewelry.title: Mundane Jewelry
mundane_jewelry.text:
Not everything I create with arcane means needs to be arcane itself. Sometimes, magic can be nothing more than a means to an end.
I've designed a few pieces of nice-looking jewelry. Their construction uses magic to take a couple of shortcuts - the proper techniques would take hours of my time.

adorned_ring.title: Adorned Ring
stages:
It's clear to me that paying attention to the quality of my equipments' construction can improve its quality noticeably.
I wonder if this applies to other things I happen to be carrying... can I improve the efficiency of my crafting simply by wearing new clothes?

Not in the sense I was expecting. Rather than reducing efficiency loss coming from the equipment itself, I can create equipment that improves the efficiency of other parts of the process.
This pretty adorned ring, for example, provides a {c3}5%{r} vis discount on all crafting and casting through clever refraction of vis away from my hands.
It's a little underwhelming, but it's a start.

research.arcana.infernal_forge.stage.1:
My new perspective has enabled me to understand the ramblings of these scribbled notes, but in the time since their creation, much has been lost.{~sep}Several records speak of a hellish device, the "In---na- F-r---e", that used the power of a Nether being to perform the thaumaturge's wishes at no cost.
Like many other entries, much of it has been torn out or burnt, but this is the earliest such page by far; and I believe that enough has been left behind for me to reconstitute its meaning, regardless of how well hidden it has been.
research.arcana.infernal_forge.stage.2:
These components, like many others sourced from the Nether, are not entirely mundane nor dead, instead holding a link to... something.
Perhaps I could put that {i}something{r} to good use.
research.arcana.infernal_forge.stage.3: This structure is designed to pull forth and capture those lost souls, but these won't work without pay. They want a sacrifice for their work, whatever it is they do, but what would satisfy them?
research.arcana.arcane_levitator.stage.1:
My vertical mobility is woefully limited. Scaling cliffs is nearly impossible, and in my own home, the most I can do is tediously lay out long-winded staircases.
There must be some magical solution I can use to making moving up and down easier.
research.arcana.arcane_levitator.stage.2:
It isn't flight, but close enough to be useful.
Any creature or item, including myself, on top of a levitator will be quickly lifted upwards. If I crouch, I'll instead be lowered downwards.
Levitators can be stacked to increase their vertical range; each provides 10 blocks, up to a total maximum of 50.
Due to their small power usage, a levitator can draw sufficient power from the surrounding aura. Doing so does cause a minuscule amount of flux to be released; while the aura should be more than able to handle a few, I can turn off ones not in use using a redstone signal.
research.arcana.levitational_locomotive.stage.1:
Ordinary carts and engines, while impressive in their own right, have a hefty infrastructure requirement. Miles and miles of tracks, with complex switching systems at every intersection or turn.
Now that I can levitate objects, I wonder if I can remove the need for such things.
research.arcana.levitational_locomotive.stage.2.1:
Replacing the wheels and tracks of a cart with tiltable levitators and ground signals may arguably make it no longer qualify as a cart. But it works better than they ever did.
A Levitational Locomotive is made up of a Suspension Engine at the front, with a line of Levitational Minecarts attached behind it. A locomotive starts stationary, and moves in a straight line, turning or stopping based on floor-placed signals. If the locomotive reaches a diagonal line of blocks (that rails could be placed on) or stairs, it will move up; otherwise, it will stop on hitting a wall.
research.arcana.levitational_locomotive.stage.2.2:
The Start/Stop signal causes the locomotive to start or stop when its engine passes over it, depending on whether the signal has redstone power (start) or not (stop).
The left-, right-, and random-turn signals will make a locomotive turn left, right, or in a random free direction. Turn signals can be disabled by redstone.
The check signal will emit a redstone pulse when an engine moves over it.
The wait signal will stop the locomotive when any *cart* containing items is placed on top, to be drained by a hopper below.
research.arcana.mystic_mist.stage.1:
Rarely, if ever, is the weather in my favour. My crops are always lacking in water, and fires are free to rage across forests from innocent-looking lava pools, while the rain annoys me when I choose to travel far away.
Should I find myself in need of it, the nearest region with snowfall may be a day's trek away - and let's not even mention the difficulty of getting lightning when you do want it.
If only I could control the weather myself... I'll need to take some readings of how altitude affects physical conditions, to better my understanding of how weather functions.
research.arcana.mystic_mist.stage.2:
Changing how the global climate functions is well outside of my reach - at least, for now.
But something more useful may be achievable: making miniature climates, say, the size of a room. Tiny clouds, exactly where I need them, precisely manipulating the conditions to perfection for myself and my crops.
research.arcana.mystic_mist.stage.3:
The Mystic Mist is a device capable of creating miniature climates as needed. When powered by essentia of the requisite type, it can create one of the following effects:
 - Creating clouds above crops to speed up their growth, above fires on flammable materials to put them out, and over empty crucibles to fill them, using {aspect:water} Aqua.
 - Creating thunderclouds above itself that can produce lightning, using {aspect:energy} Potentia.
 - Creating blizzard clouds above itself that produce snowfall, using {aspect:ice} Gelum.
 - Creating a hot, dry environment around itself, suitable for the growth of Nether Wart and proliferation of fire (should I need it), using {aspect:fire} Ignis.
research.arcana.monocle_of_revealing.stage.1:
Wearing the Goggles of Revealing is essentially a requirement for doing any kind of magical work - yet doing so prevents me from wearing important protected headwear.
A more lightweight and compatible form would be appreciated.
research.arcana.monocle_of_revealing.stage.2:
Reducing the goggles to a single lens does suffice for casual use.
It takes a bit of squinting, but the Monocles of Revealing are just as capable for alchemy or peering into nodes as the full-sized goggles, but only take up a trinkets slot.
I do wonder what other improvements could be made to the goggles, though...
research.arcana.auromancy_root.text:
The study of {i}auromancy{r}, the manipulation of the aura and vis around me, will be documented here.
The iron and gold wand caps, greatwood wand core, and the general wand recipe are included here for completeness.
research.arcana.wand_components.text:
Every wand is constructed from wand caps and a core, which dictate it's properties.{~sep}The core is responsible for storing vis. The more vis a core can store, the more I can use it to perform arcane crafting, and the more powerful the items I craft can be.
The cap is responsible for channeling and shaping that vis. They affect the speed in which vis is drawn from nodes, and adds a small amount of vis storage.
Both components also affect spellcasting through foci. A wand has a "complexity" score, based on the quality of its cap, that determines how complex the effects it produces can be. More powerful foci may require higher complexities, and modifications made to foci may only apply if a certain complexity is met.
Wands also have a "difficulty" score, given by their cores, that determines how much "force" it can push the vis with. The same focus may provide stronger effects - like more damage or healing - with a higher difficulty wand.
Finally, some caps and cores may provide additional side effects, like discounts or bonuses, depending on what they're made from. I might want to use different wands for different tasks.
research.arcana.copper_wand_caps.stage.1: The properties of copper make it quite convenient for electrical work. It's conductivity and alignment with Instrumentum may make it a highly useful material in my artifice.
research.arcana.copper_wand_caps.stage.2: Wand caps crafted from copper are slightly worse than gold when it comes to drawing vis from nodes, or focusing them into spells, but come with a useful bonus to difficulty.
research.arcana.leather_wand_caps.stage.1:
While metals are an obvious go-to for channelling vis, I should experiment with other, more flexible materials.
Having a greater degree of control over the shape and design of the cap might allow me to produce something more efficient.
research.arcana.leather_wand_caps.stage.2:
Wand caps crafted from leather are slightly worse than gold when it comes to drawing vis form nodes, or focusing them into spells, but do provide a decent bonus to arcane crafting.
Any wand strapped with leather reduces the amount of vis required to craft by {c3}8%{r}.
research.arcana.nether_stem_wand_core.stage.1:
Fungi do not seem to be a traditional wand material by any stretch. Certainly, none of the notes even seemed to consider the possibility.
But the huge mushrooms of the nether may provide some unique properties, different to everything available in the overworld.
research.arcana.nether_stem_wand_core.stage.2:
Nether stems are simple enough to craft into capable wand cores, and perform much better than ordinary untreated wood.
While it doesn't perform better than I would expect a magical wood to, it's complex internal structures grant wands constructed from nether stems a bonus to complexity.
research.arcana.varnished_wood_wand_core.stage.1: Simply using a stick of mundane wood for a wand core has predictably poor results. Part of this can be attributed to poor material qualities, but I wonder how much of this is caused by lack of effort in its preparation?
research.arcana.varnished_wood_wand_core.stage.2:
By properly treating the wood before use, and paying additional attention to it's design, the Varnished Wood wand core performs much better than its untreated counterpart.
While it doesn't perform better than I would expect a magical wood to, it does come with a useful discount in arcane crafting. Any varnished wooden wand reduces the amount of vis required to craft by {c3}12%{r}.
research.arcana.silverwood_wand_core.stage.1:
The use of greatwood as a wand core has been a great success, but it is by no means the end-all. Surely silverwood, known for its special relationship with nodes and the aura, will be able to outdo it.
For many of the notes' authors, silverwood was considered the peak of wand design, with many leaving their studies there.
Unfortunately, silverwood is both highly delicate, and highly sensitive to changes in the surrounding aura. Transforming it into a high-capacity wand core will not be a trivial task.
research.arcana.silverwood_wand_core.stage.2:
Analyzing these samples has taught me a couple of things:
 - Silverwood rods are flimsy, too fragile to channel the intense vis I need.
 - Very little of the wood has any special properties to begin with, only within some internal transport network.
Perhaps the trees have diverged over the years, or I'm missing some crucial information on how they are put together, but regardless, I'll need to try something different to build this.
research.arcana.silverwood_wand_core.stage.3:
Alchemy seems to be the answer. With it, I can dissolve away the useless bulk of the wood, increase its strength, and accentuate all of its useful properties.
While this is certainly better than every material I've tried so far, it doesn't nearly live up to the expectations given by the notes. Indeed, they seem to refer to a completely different, multi-step process instead, which may lead to better results.
Silverwood wands have high capacities and difficulty scores, but no special effects.
research.arcana.sugar_cane_wand_core.stage.1: There remains a wide variety of plants to which I can apply my alchemical technique. Perhaps they might offer some unique benefits.
research.arcana.sugar_cane_wand_core.stage.2:
Wands made with sugar cane have a special affinity with {aspect:air}, granting a {c3}15%{r} discount for it in arcane crafting.
Otherwise, they're somewhat weaker than silverwood cores.
research.arcana.blaze_wand_core.stage.1:
While fungi were a good start, other nether materials may prove useful.
Blaze rods are already roughly the right shape, and lend themselves to alchemy in other forms.
research.arcana.blaze_wand_core.stage.2:
Wands made with blaze rods have a special affinity with {aspect:fire}, granting a {c3}15%{r} discount for it in arcane crafting.
Otherwise, they're somewhat weaker than silverwood cores.
research.arcana.ice_wand_core.stage.1:
I wonder what the limits of my technique are.
If solidity and some kind of conduction are all that's necessary, can translucent ice be used?
research.arcana.ice_wand_core.stage.2:
Wands made with ice have a special affinity with {aspect:water}, granting a {c3}15%{r} discount in it for arcane crafting.
Otherwise, they're somewhat weaker than silverwood cores.
It's worth noting that these cores also have an affinity with {aspect:ice}, {aspect:crystal}, and {aspect:light}, but these have no applications in arcane crafting nor spellcasting.
The alchemy applied prevents the wand from ever melting, but it doesn't prevent my hand from getting painfully cold.
research.arcana.obsidian_wand_core.stage.1: Obsidian is a tough material, and in certain circumstances, can naturally carry magic of its own. It should make for a solid wand core.
research.arcana.obsidian_wand_core.stage.2:
Wands made with crying obsidian have a special affinity with {aspect:earth}, granting a {c3}15%{r} discount in it for arcane crafting.
Surprisingly, it's own magical properties only hinder thaumaturgy, leaving it a little weaker than a silverwood core. Further research will be necessary...
research.arcana.arcane_stone_wand_core.stage.1: So far, using materials that already have an arcane touch has lead to my best results. How far does this go? Can a material as simple as arcane stone be used effectively?
research.arcana.arcane_stone_wand_core.stage.2:
The crystal structure within arcane stone makes it a useful wand core; wands made with it have a special affinity with {aspect:order}, and grant a {c3}15%{r} discount in it for arcane crafting.
They perform worse than silverwood, though, as is to be expected.
research.arcana.bone_wand_core.stage.1:
Living things can never be entirely mundane. Every breath and dream leaves a mark on the body, and sometimes, that is just enough for it to refuse death, for just a moment.
I have no intention of messing with mortality; but I do wonder if this leftover power can be useful to me in any way.
research.arcana.bone_wand_core.stage.2:
Wands made from bone have a special affinity with {aspect:entropy}, granting a {c3}15%{r} discount in it for arcane crafting.
Otherwise, they're somewhat weaker than silverwood cores.
They also serve as a sombering reminder of my own mortality, a topic I prefer not to think about.
research.arcana.wand_foci.stage.1:
Wands are excellent, portable batteries of vis, useful for careful crafting of magical devices. But to perform even more powerful magic, dedicated focuses for their primal vis will be required.
The notes include a huge variety of designs for these, reflecting their importance in everyday thaumaturgy. Some are barely more than focused primal vis, while others combine and shape them in ways that break the ordinary laws of reality; others still use materials beyond my imagination to perform dangerous feats of insanity.
For my first, I will stick to the absolute basics: focusing ignis vis to create fire.
research.arcana.wand_foci.stage.2:
When a wand has a wand focus equipped, right-clicking will attempt to cast the focus. The fire focus will simply set blocks and living creatures on fire.
I can equip a focus by holding a wand and pressing a key - usually {c3}G{r} - to open the focus switcher. Clicking or hovering over a focus in the outer ring will equip it, while clicking on the middle equipped focus will remove it.
As outlined in {c3}Caps and Cores{r}, foci may require a wand of a certain complexity, and their power may depend on the wand's difficulty. This focus can be cast with any basic wand; the amount of fire damage dealt to creatures, and their time on fire, depends on the wand's difficulty.
Casting using a focus takes some vis from the wand. This amount is affected by discounts in the same way as arcane crafting; the original amount is displayed in the focus tooltip, while the discounted amount is displayed in the wand's (when equipped).

focus_pouch.title: Focus Storge
stages: As my arsenal of foci grows, so will my power, and so will my inventory handling woes. Letting 10 different glorified marbles clink around in my inventory is perhaps not the best use of space... I should nip this problem in the bud early.

Specialised to storing wand foci, a Focus Pouch provides 27 additional slots that can be accessed directly from a wand's focus switcher, which becomes specialized to use it.
The pouch's inventory is split between a row of {i}quick-access{r} slots, and two more of storage slots. The focus switcher will only show quick-access foci, and maintain their position when switching foci. Foci in storage (or elsewhere in my inventory) will appear below.
I can move between the quick-access and storage rows with tab, and use the number keys to quickly select foci.

research.arcana.light_focus.stage.1:
One of the most tedious things of my journey, by far, has been carrying around enough torches and light sources for everywhere I go; wasting my inventory space and ending exploration or mining sessions prematurely.
Ideally, I could simply point at a spot with my wand, mention a spell, and have a light source spring forth. Like a real magician.
research.arcana.light_focus.stage.2:
This focus creates light sources using stored aer and ignis, fused to make lux.
These light sources are temporary, losing brightness over time until they fade away entirely, making them sadly unsuitable for anything permanent. Perhaps some invisible nitor could suit that role? But they don't require any space or special considerations on-the-go, so I consider this a success.
Initially, a light source is as bright as glowstone - brighter than a torch - and dims until it is unable to repel monsters, before vanishing, and can also be broken by hand. They can be placed underwater without issue.
research.arcana.portable_hole_focus.stage.1:
The ender pearl and chorus fruit have a curious ability to warp space.
These naturally occurring materials do it in a raw, unfocused form; with some careful manipulation, and the added power of the wand's vis, something much safer and more powerful should be possible.
research.arcana.portable_hole_focus.stage.2:
I don't really understand how this works.
I went into this expecting to create a teleportation focus, but rather than moving me through space, this focus changes the space around me. When used against a surface, the focus temporarily phases it, and everything behind it, out of existence, allowing me to pass through walls and into caves.
The focus creates 3x3 tunnels that can reach at least {c3}12{r} blocks in length, and even further with a higher difficulty wand, but end when they reach a full square of air. They can be oriented in any direction, including vertically.
Any block can be phased out, including containers, and blocks that support other blocks. Such systems remain fully stable; for all intents and purposes, those blocks still exist, except for entities to look and pass through. Space is warped, but matter is untouched.
As a more demanding wand focus, this requires a higher complexity than what an iron wand cap can provide alone.
I would do well to research the structure of space in more detail. Some other time.
research.arcana.equivalent_exchange_focus.stage.1:
When parts of the world are phased out, although I can move through that space, new blocks can't be put in their place.
While it makes sense - the matter all still exists - it {i}would{r} be convenient to be able to quickly replace blocks in the world through other means, for easy construction and refurbishment.
research.arcana.equivalent_exchange_focus.stage.2:
This new focus simply instantly breaks the block I look at, replacing it with whichever block is in my off-hand.
Derived from diamond, the focus can destroy any block breakable by diamond; the casting cost scales with the mining level of the block I try to replace, up to {c3}3x{r} for anything demanding diamond tools.

prismatic_light_focus.title: Wand Focus: Prismatic Light
stages: It's about time I put together some proper magical weaponry - there's no good reason for me to {i}still{r} be swinging around glorified sticks, not when I could be raining pure destructive energy down from afar. No, not anymore.

Unlike simpler foci, the focus of prismatic light takes a moment to charge, building up an orb of interleaved light. After dropping my concentration, the orb will fly in the direction I look, bursting on contact and damaging anything that gets too close; the larger I let it get, the stronger that burst.
Obviously, the undead are particularly susceptible, but anything will fall with enough strikes.

research.arcana.alchemy_root.text:
The study of {i}alchemy{r}, the conversion of items into essentia and utilization thereof, will be documented here.
The Nitor recipe from {c3}Fundamentals{r} is included here for completeness.

magical_metallurgy.title: Magical Metallurgy
stages:
Mundane materials just aren't cutting it anymore.
Tools break too quickly, armour doesn't protect well enough, and these materials simply aren't as conductive to the arcane crafts as I would like.
The notes often reference a material named {u}Thaumium{r}, created by alchemically imbuing a metal with magic itself. I don't know what their metallurgy was like - it seems that the set of ores available to me differ to what they had - but the principle seems sound.

This isn't thaumium. At least, not like they described. Some of its properties persist, but blindingly bright, shedding its contained magic over time... maybe I overshot somewhat.
All the usual tool and armour recipes work, producing equipment with an enchantability and mining speed above mundane gold or diamond, with a toughness slightly above iron.
Entire blocks can be transmuted, at a slight discount.

addenda.set_bonus.name: Arcane Aura
addenda.set_bonus.text:
When wearing a full set of armour made from this metal, the magic radiating from it becomes physical, almost.
This effect, Arcane Aura, boosts the strength of my spells.

research.arcana.transmutation.stage.1:
One popular trope is that of an alchemist attempting to create the valuable from the dull - lead to gold. They knew neither chemistry nor magic; I know both.
I believe I can use my newfound knowledge to do better at the transmutation of metals.
research.arcana.transmutation.stage.2: Converting iron into copper is not my most impressive achievement - though the alchemy behind this recipe {wavy}does{r} prompt more research into it's properties. No, gold is my target. Though copper may make a useful stepping stone...
research.arcana.transmutation.stage.3:
Yes! Where thousands of fictional alchemists have failed, I have succeeded in transforming iron into gold.
I do wonder if the process is reversible, though... or could be performed in bulk.
research.arcana.transmutation.stage.4:
The transmutations form a loop: iron into copper, copper into gold, and gold into iron. Could be useful given a particular shortage of iron.. perhaps if I was into mundane science.
What's also interesting is that each of these recipes can be applied in block form, at a slight discount.
research.arcana.purification.stage.1:
Simply baking ores and letting the metal melt out is an immensely inefficient process. Crushing the ores might be less so, but would still leave me waiting twice as long to process them. I have a better idea.
With alchemy, it should be possibly to wash away the stone and all other impurities, and leave behind a pure structure of metal to be melted into ingots all at once.
...I just need to figure out how.
research.arcana.purification.stage.2:
This is certainly one way of doing it.
The aspects added reinforce the metal's structure, with the extra metallum acting as a substitute for the impurities. This does mean that some metal is required as input, and some of the input is still wasted, but I could not find a better way around it.
Now, to apply this to other metals. With luck, there should be no nasty surprises awaiting me.
research.arcana.purification.stage.3:
Copper and gold can be purified and cast in exactly the same manner as iron; their disparate properties seem to have had no effect on the process.
Additionally, the process can be applied in bulk to raw metal blocks, at a slight discount.
research.arcana.transmutation_shortcut.text:
Extending my transmutation knowledge to purified metal turned out to be surprisingly trivial.
All transmutation recipes work on alchemical metal for the cost of a single ingot.
research.arcana.metallurgy_shortcut.text:
Extending my metallurgy knowledge to purified metal turned out to be surprisingly trivial.
Alchemical gold can be converted to Altered Gold for the cost of a single arcanium ingot. Altered gold can then be smelted to produce two arcanium ingots at once.
research.arcana.alumentum.stage.1:
Nitor was a start, but its stability makes it useless as a fuel, barely warm enough to heat a crucible; I'd be better off using a campfire than trying to make that work.
No, what I need is something far more energetic and excitable, only stable enough to transport to a blast furnace; perhaps it could even double as a weapon...
research.arcana.alumentum.stage.2:
And Alumentum is the solution. Like nitor, it is a never-ending flame, but this one can only barely keep itself together.
As a fuel, it should last about {c3}4x{r} as good as coal.
If I throw it, it will violently explode upon hitting a surface. I should take great care handling this... or not, depending on where I find myself.
research.arcana.hedge_alchemy.stage.1:
There are a great few items that are incredibly tedious to obtain, in constant short supply when I need them most. Perhaps I can use alchemy to create them?
My first step will be to examine some samples, and find similar structures that can - fingers crossed - be converted into eachother.
research.arcana.hedge_alchemy.stage.2:
From my observation, {i}Gunpowder{r} is closely alchemically related to {i}Blaze Powder{r}; {i}Redstone{r} and {i}Glowstone{r} have similar structures; and {i}Quartz{r} has an odd (but promising) resemblance to {i}Diamond{r}. The Lava was a dud.
I believe I can alchemy to emulate more mundane reactions: tanning {i}Rotten Flesh{r} into {i}Leather{r}, freezing {i}Snow{r} into {i}Ice{r}, drying {i}Leaves{r} into {i}Dead Bushes{r}, and binding {i}String{r} into {i}Cobwebs{r}.
Some experimental verification is needed.
research.arcana.hedge_alchemy.stage.3:
Most of these conversions are viable alchemy recipes. Quartz-to-diamond was a dud too, simply turning into flint in any practical setting, and converting snow into ice proved far less efficient than expected.
Could this be due to my equipment, or my technique? Perhaps, but in any case, the remainder remain useful.

taint_in_a_bottle.title: Containing Taint
stages: Taint is dangerous and eager to spread. Given even a small amount of flux, it will poison the land around it startlingly fast. Perhaps alchemy could be used to contain it? First, I'll attempt to seal some into a bottle, and in the future I can construct a more general solution.

...the applications of this are limited at best, and dangerous at worst. When Taint in a Bottle is thrown and hits a surface, it instantly taints up to six nearby blocks, and releases some flux.
As a weapon, the bottles are dangerous, but also expensive. Tainting a large area would require quite a few bottles, but would also render that area uninhabitable for quite some time...
I could collect the blocks for further study, but I don't believe I can get a net profit of Virimus, and placing them will render them eager to spread once more.
I don't see any practical uses of this. Only a mad scientist would mass produce this.

research.arcana.automated_alchemy.stage.1: There's nothing particularly remarkable about alchemy.{~sep}Sure, it takes a bit of know-how to figure out which reactions are possible, and gently guide the liquid concepts in the pot to approach that. But really, what's stopping me from simply... teaching a dropper how to do it?
research.arcana.automated_alchemy.stage.2: Prototype after prototype wasted. Something odd is afoot here. Even getting a machine to perform identical actions to myself does not cause the proper reactions. Almost like some {i}intent{r} is necessary.
research.arcana.automated_alchemy.stage.3: Now, a thinking machine. That would do it.
research.arcana.automated_alchemy.stage.4:
Giving a Dropper a basic level of "understanding" is a perfectly safe and simple method of automating alchemy.
The Aware Dropper can be given a Tome of Sharing within it's extra tenth slot. Items it drops will be eligible for any alchemy recipes stored within the research bound to the book. When an alchemy recipe is performed automatically, the result will be thrown from the crucible in a random, free horizontal direction (or just randomly if none are free).
Another minor feature is that these droppers have slightly less variation in how they drop items.
It turns out that Tomes of Sharing do remember research entries, but simply choose not to show them to players. The thought of my equipment colluding to snoop on my mind is unsettling... but what can a book really do?
research.arcana.alchemical_glass.stage.1:
Glass is a wonderful substance. Unreactive, transparent, commonly available... and extremely flimsy.
Correcting mistakes while should not require specialist equipment, and I wouldn't put too much trust in ordinary glass as a component in my devices.
Some upgrades are in order.
research.arcana.alchemical_glass.stage.2:
The first fruits of my work come in the form of Hardened Glass. Stronger - resisting explosions and less prone to accidents - yet more resilient - dropping itself in one piece when broken.
I do have questions about what other properties I can give to glass this way... how about making it even more conductive to light and vis?
research.arcana.alchemical_glass.stage.3:
As-is, glass isn't much more opaque than empty space. No, the interesting part is when you allow it to capture light and vis.
Luminiferous Glass, while appearing transparent, has a huge amount of photons and lux captured within. On the outside, this manifests as a bright glow, on par with Glowstone. In the future, a material like this will be useful to use as a component in magical devices.
Now, I wonder if it's possible to make glass conductive to not just energy, but matter. Would it simply fall through the crucible? Is it even a well-formed question?
research.arcana.alchemical_glass.stage.4:
...apparently, yes, this is fully possible.
Static Glass is usually solid, but becomes like a gas in the presence of a crouching player - allowing their passage (or fall) - before reforming into a solid.
This has a couple of potential applications in home decor. Artifice? Perhaps, if I can trigger it mechanically.

essentia_distillation.title: Essentia Distillation
stages:
I believe it is now time to tackle the challenge of essentia: concentrating vis into a potent, liquid form.{~sep}What little the past authors had detailed varies wildly, and I believe I am on my own to reinvent the process. Alchemy is a good starting position - it involves essentia in some form or other - but is much too crude, too unrefined.
Alchemy relies heavily on the use of water to distribute heat, provide a medium for aspects to flow, and mix them evenly. Invaluable there, but that mixing and contamination precludes its use here; perhaps my newly discovered materials can make up for it with even more heat?
I have a couple of theories already; not much more to do than put them to the test.

That... was a catastrophic failure. The essentia began to form, but refused to properly separate from the object, no matter how hot or intense it became - finally vaporizing into flux, and the few leftovers crystalizing.{~sep}Surely it's fixable? Maybe another object could be used to draw out the essentia, as is done in alchemy?

As it turns out, I need to do precisely the opposite: provide some "filler" to {i}force{r} the essentia {i}out{r} of the item.
The final design I have landed on is superficially similar to the scraps left behind. An {i}Arcane Furnace{r} melts items down into an indeterminate slurry, while {i}Alembics{r} stacked above it further distil the slurry into essentia.
The furnace requires both fuel for heat, and a substrate to push out essentia. Items with a very small amount of aspects will burn quicker, and denser objects will settle at about 2 seconds each.
The fuel can be anything that burns in an ordinary furnace, and lasts just as long; the substrate is used up as aspects are purified, and can limit melting rate. Once any item is burned, it leaves behind a {i}Shattered Husk{r} that must be eventually removed to avoid clogging up the machine.
For now, the only substrate I have available are primal crystals, which can account for {c3}5{r} essentia each; finding more efficient substrates is a priority.
Alembics placed above a furnace will draw out slurry from its internal buffer and convert it into essentia. Each alembic can store up to {c3}100{r} of any single aspect.

essentia_transport.title: Essentia Transport
stages:
Handling essentia requires special preparation and equipment; no ordinary bucket or bottle will do, let alone leaving it out in the open.{~sep}For manual transfer, I can use {i}Phials{r}. These small enchanted bottles store exactly {c3}8{r} of any aspect, and can be filled or emptied into blocks simply by right clicking.
To store essentia in larger quantities, I can use {i}Warded Jars{r}. These blocks store up to {c3}100{r} of any single aspect, and visually show their aspect and fullness. When broken, they drop themselves and hold onto their contained essentia.

Of course, I would prefer to automate transportation wherever possible. Dispensers are capable of using phials just fine, but dedicated blocks are much more effective.
{i}Essentia Tubes{r} transport essentia that has been pushed into them. In tubes, essentia takes the form of tiny {i}specks{r}, which move along at their own speed and direction, weakly obey gravity, and otherwise only change directions when they hit a wall. I should experiment with them to get familiar with their behaviour.
Tubes don't take essentia out of blocks like jars and alembics on their own, however; I'll need to use {i}Aspect Pumps{r}, a variation of tubes that pulls out essentia from the indicated direction. Pumps can be disabled using a redstone signal, and given an essentia phial to filter them to just one aspect.
For more control over their movement, I can also use {i}Aspect Valves{r} to open and close routes, which can be toggled by hand or redstone. Finally, to get a rough look at essentia flow, I can use {i}Essentia Windows{r}; these flash the colour of incoming essentia for a short period. A glowing window emits a comparator signal.

crystal_curator.title: Crystal Curator
stages:
It seems strange that essentia should come in every aspect imaginable, while the crystals I find around the world would restrict themselves to the primals.
Are the compound aspects simply not stable enough to crystallize? Or does their absence from the aura preclude their {i}natural{r} formation only?
Simply knowing would be a significant achievement. And as a bonus, if I can figure out how to crystallize essentia myself, having easy control over compound aspects is sure to open up many new applications. Crystal formation is a tricky thing worth studying.

A really, {i}really{r} tricky thing.
Gemstones and aspect crystals form through different pathways: the former using extreme heat and pressure, the latter an overflow in the aura. Manipulating the aura is a no-go, at least for now, but compacting essentia in a controlled burst seems to do the trick for tiny crystals.
Now to make them grow to a usable size.

Essentia distillation turns solid matter into essentia, through much effort. You'd think the reverse should be simpler, but clearly not.
A Crystallization Press is a specially-designed block capable of forcing essentia into a solid form. It requires quartz crystals as a "seed", with each providing for {c3}12{r} new aspect crystals, as well as the essentia to crystallize. Each crystal requires {c3}2{r} points of essentia: this is a wasteful process, which should be totally unsurprising given the methodology.

essentia_logistics.title: Essentia Logistics
essentia_logistics.desc: It's not like I'm in a hurry or anything
stages: Setting up essentia networks can be tedious. Just incredibly tedious. I just want to move the fundamental concepts of reality from point A to point B, why the issue? And why must it clog up so easily?

As a nice convenience, an {i}Aspect Redirect{r} forces all specks entering to travel in one direction; and an {i}Aspect Router{r} splits specks across all other connected directions, randomly. These let me skip or compact some otherwise-complicated setups... but these {i}are{r} fairly expensive.
Additionally, I can create specially-configured {i}Void Jars{r} that continue to accept essentia when full, venting excess essentia into the aura; by which I mean as flux. It's certainly easier than carefully managing my essentia production, but it's not something I should overuse.

substrate_synthesis.title: Substrate Synthesis
stages:
As established, I need to find substrates more efficient than the primal aspect crystals, which require a handful to break down even moderately complex objects.
Many substances can be used as mundane fillers, and I believe altering one may allow for creating a powerful substrate.

Providing something too dense with any single aspect produces a low-quality substrate, but binding multiple together with {aspect:slime} Gelum produces something much more effective. Indeed, mundane slime is almost sufficient already, though some magic will enhance it much further.
By combining magical and mundane ingredients, I can produce Synthetic Scaffolding, a more efficient distillation substrate. Each of these can account for {c3}15{r} essentia each.

purifying_enchantment.title: Arcane Enchantment: Purifying
stages:
The process of metal purification, while useful, still has some slightly inefficiencies. More importantly, it is inconvenient to need to lug back piles of raw ores from mining expeditions only to find myself with another pile of tedium to attend to. Bulk processing aids this somewhat, but the best shortcut would be to combine the two steps entirely: my pickaxe should perform alchemy for me.
Now equipped with the ability to purify and manipulate essentia directly, I believe this should be possible, potentially even easy. The medium of enchanting provides a means to apply precise effects to otherwise-mundane tools; an essentia coating should work just as well.

Mimicking the structure of other mining enchantments leads to a straightforward recipe for a {i}Purifying{r} enchantment, which causes raw ore drops to be randomly transmuted into their purified, alchemical forms. The chance begins at 20%, and is multiplied by the enchantment's level, up to 3.
Entire stacks are transmuted at once. If a block would drop multiple of an item, the chance is divided by the size of the stack.

transmutative_enchantment.title: Arcane Enchantment: Transmutative
stages: I've studied far much varied alchemy than simply purifying metals. It would be interesting to see what might happen with more varied, less controlled transmutative magic applied to a weapon.

Following the same formula Purifying, I arrive at {i}Transmutative{r}, which replaces mob drops with transmuted variants. These transmutations include most recipes from Hedge Alchemy, with a number of additional, more unpredictable ones.
Unlike Purifying, these transmutations are guaranteed.

introduction.title: introduction.
introduction.text:
we have all seen things that we might not want to have seen. we have all found out some piece of critical info that doesn't fit our worldview. perhaps something as magical as a revelation from beyond, or mundane as a broken heart.
whatever it is that lead you to the crimson, you're welcome here. you will be useful here. you will feel the fulfillment you deserve.

initiation.title: initiation.
stages:
every page that sits in front of you is filled with difficult truths. such ideas require time to acclimate, time to swallow the concepts this world had worked hard to keep from your mind.
before the truth may be revealed to you, you must prove yourself ready. to simply reveal everything at once would leave insufficient time to explain, would let those hammered-in worms of restraint keep you from Understanding. your first exercise will be trivial, just a small show of commitment.
you will make for such a useful follower.

force_of_space.title: forces of space.
force_of_space.text:
the world is truly, truly vast, and even it is not alone in the cosmos. the size of it seems insurmountable, but we are numerous, we the Truthseekers that must discover and liberate it all.
you, too, must become a Truthseeker. become a cartographer, become an astronomer, study the space around you - together, we may someday discover it all.

force_of_time.title: forces of time.
force_of_time.text:
the world is ancient. every living creature has an enormous lineage; every civilisation had their own predecessors, and among {i}their{r} predecessors were historians trying to understand the Beginning.
you are still quite early in your journey, but it is no well-kept secret that our reality has had a turbulent past. civilisations rose and fell not just by eachothers' hands, but by the whims of a shifting- changing- melding- twisting kind of Magic. entirely random at a first glance, its progression becomes clear with more knowledge - and yet more worrisome.
following this path forward, we find a dead future. a reality that not only loses its magic, but one that loses {u}life{r} itself, one where no intelligent beings could speak and thrive. tracing it back into the past, a strange picture of the Beginning starts to emerge; but one yet contradictory and vague.
you must make it your duty to discover the past, to complete these blanks, and - through our shared achievements - perhaps avert the calamitous future that awaits.
